wu: Family Chain: Students stand in a circle, one starts by saying 'This is my mother', the next says 'This is my mother, this is my father', continuing until someone forgets. They sit down, last one standing wins.
wuAlt: Flashcard Speed: Show family flashcards quickly, students shout the English word. Wrong answer = sit down.
Draw & Guess: One student draws a family member (e.g., brother), others guess 'Is this your brother?'
pres: Use a large family tree poster with photos of a Moroccan family (include mother, father, sister, brother, baby). Model sentences: 'This is my mother. She is 35. She has got long hair.' Point to each person, ask 'Who is this?' and elicit answers. Check with thumbs up/down if they understand.
presAlt: Bring in a real family photo album (yours or a colleague's), describe each person using the target language.
Use a short animated story about a family, pause to introduce vocabulary and model sentences.
prac: Family Tree Match: In pairs, students get cut-out family member pictures and labels. They match pictures to labels (mother, father, etc.) and say 'This is my...'. Monitor and correct pronunciation. Support by pre-teaching pronunciation with phonics drills (e.g., 'bro-ther' /'brʌðər/).
pracAlt: Bingo: Students draw a 3x3 grid and write 5 family words. Teacher calls out words, first to complete shouts 'Bingo!' and says the sentences.
Chain Drill: Teacher says 'This is my mother', student 1 repeats and adds 'This is my father', student 2 repeats both and adds 'This is my sister', etc.
ls: Listen and Draw: Students get a blank family tree. Teacher describes a family: 'This is my father. He is 40. This is my mother. She has got glasses.' Students draw and label. Check by having them hold up their trees and compare in pairs.
re: Family Charades: One student acts out a family member (e.g., rocking a baby for 'baby'), others guess 'Is this your brother?' or 'Is this your mother?'. Fast and physical to re-energize.
prod: Family Roleplay: In pairs, students get props (toy phone, baby doll). One calls the other, introduces their family: 'Hello! This is my sister. She is 8. This is my baby. He is 1.' They take turns. Present to the class for stickers.
rw: Read and Complete: Students read a short text about a family (e.g., 'My name is Fatima. This is my father. He is a teacher. This is my mother. She is a doctor.'). They complete a simple family tree diagram with names and ages.
st: Story: Read 'The Very Busy Family' by Pat Hutchins, focusing on family actions. Sing 'If You're Happy and You Know It' with family actions (clap your hands for 'father', stomp your feet for 'mother'). End with Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Family Memory
Place family flashcards face down. Students turn two over, say 'This is my mother' if they match.
Guess Who?
Teacher describes a family member (e.g., 'He is tall. He is my father.'), students guess who it is.
Family Pictionary
One student draws a family member, others guess 'Is this your sister?'
Family Survey
Students walk around asking 'How old is your mother?' and tally answers on a chart.
Family Tree Race
In teams, race to label a large family tree poster with the correct words.
Family Bingo
Students listen to descriptions and mark the correct family member on their bingo card.
Family Charades
Students act out family members for others to guess.
Family Chain
Students take turns adding a family member to a sentence chain.
Family Match
Students match family member pictures to words in a timed race.
Family Quiz
Teacher asks questions like 'Who is the baby?', students answer with 'This is my baby.'
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write 3 extra sentences about their family (e.g., 'My father likes football').
Support / weaker learners: Use a word bank with family words and sentence starters to describe their tree.
hw: Interview your family member: Ask 'How old are you?' and 'What is your job?'. Write 2 answers in your notebook.
Draw your family tree and label 5 members in English.
Write 3 sentences about your family: 'This is my... He/She is... years old.'
tip: Use local family structures (e.g., including grandparents) to make the theme relatable. Praise effort with stickers to build confidence, as Moroccan learners may be shy to speak.
